title: Short-Sale Daily Accrual Calculation Clause
content:
## Short-sale daily accrual: calculation clause (Payoff and Loan Satisfaction)

On the payoff case of an Approved Short Sale Payoff requested by the borrower of record, the short-sale daily accrual is the short-sale accrual basis times the loan's daily accrual rate for a short sale, rounded half up to the cent and only at that last step.

(a) *Daily accrual rate for a short sale.* The loan's note rate plus, for a HECM, the annual MIP rate of its payout plan, divided by 100 and by the plan's per diem day count; a Summit loan carries no MIP.

(b) *Short-sale accrual basis.* The loan's principal balance plus six carried advances: the short-sale set-aside carry, the short-sale securing carry, the short-sale maintenance carry, the short-sale called-due appraisal carry, the short-sale replacement appraisal carry and the short-sale foreclosure carry.

(c) *Carried advances.* The short-sale set-aside carry, the short-sale securing carry, the short-sale maintenance carry, the short-sale replacement appraisal carry and the short-sale foreclosure carry are each 0.00, and the short-sale called-due appraisal carry is USD 475.00.

(d) *Rounding.* Only the final product of (b) and (a) is rounded, half up to the cent.

**Hypothetical worked figure.** A Summit loan with a principal balance of USD 320000.00 and a note rate of 7.25 percent, with a 365-day count from the plan schedule: rate 7.25 divided by 100 and by 365; basis USD 320000.00 plus USD 475.00, so USD 320475.00; accrual USD 63.6560 before rounding, USD 63.66 after. A HECM with the same balance, a note rate of 6.75 percent and an annual MIP rate of 0.5 percent reaches the same rate and the same USD 63.66. Invented figures.
